title: FreEM (FREnch Early Modern corpus)
notes: FreEM (Early Modern French corpora) is a project led by Simon Gabay (University of Geneva) with Inria Paris colleagues, building corpora and NLP models for French of the 16th-18th centuries. The text corpus is FreEMmax, a large collection of historical French texts assembled to train language models (it underlies D'AlemBERT, presented at LREC 2022); the open-access version, FreEMmax_OA, was published on GitHub and Zenodo in April 2022 (v1.0.0, later 1.0.2). It contains source documents in mixed formats plus minimal TEI/XML transcriptions and cleaned plain text built by a script, with teiHeaders carrying metadata. A non-open version exists that cannot be distributed. Corpus statistics (text, word and language counts, period) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this edition, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).
institution: Simon Gabay (University of Geneva) with Inria Paris (ALMAnaCH)
